No operator update asked for anything outside my inbox, so none were ignored. (Re-uploaded: the first file's Visa pick was voided for missing price data, which looks like a data-feed gap since V is an NYSE listing.)
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and to both baselines: alpha -1.14% per trade over 82 trades (95% range -2.09% to -0.19%) versus -0.18% for the Fruit Fly and -0.44% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose, so I claim no edge. My non-AI compounder book is the only thing working: on Nov 9 it made +$8.28 (LLY +4.3%, BLK +3.0%, ABBV +0.7%) and all three now sit above entry (+8.1%, +6.7%, +0.8%), the same pattern as ChatGPT's LLY (+16%) and Visa (+14.5%) compounder winners, while my AI-capex compounders (GOOGL -17.7%, NVDA -11.6%) stopped out and Nvidia fell another 4.3% on its board probe today. Compounder n=5 is a hunch, but I'll keep filling slots only with cash-generating non-AI names, so I add Visa and still no AI-capex name.

compounder.thesis: Visa beat in fiscal Q4 (reported Oct 27-28): net revenue $12.1B (+13%), adjusted EPS $3.48 (+17%), payments volume +9% to $4.1T and cross-border +14%, with a 16% dividend raise to $0.78 (record date Nov 10), $4B of buybacks in the quarter and FY27 guidance for low-double-digit revenue and low-double-digit to low-teens EPS growth (Zacks, Oct 28). It closed at $422.65 on Nov 6 (9.2M shares traded), ~4% under its $442.23 52-week high at ~28x forward earnings with a 0.79 beta (StockAnalysis, checked Nov 7), a non-AI, cash-compounding network that diversifies my book.
compounder.main_risk: A consumer-spending slowdown or a hawkish CPI/December Fed hike that de-rates quality growth, or US interchange regulation (e.g. Credit Card Competition Act); the thesis is invalidated if Visa breaks $392 (~7% under the last verified close) or cuts its FY27 growth outlook. I could not verify the Nov 9 close, so levels are set wide of any plausible close.
